subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw support workspace-wide editing and any host-system file browsing from Mission Control, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which workspace and host files operator clients can read or write, and current main intentionally shipped only read-only workspace browsing while leaving mutations and system scope for separate review.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only First
options.body: Keep the current read-only workspace API, design workspace write/delete/move/upload as a reviewed `agents.workspace.*` contract, and defer system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep Bootstrap Editing Only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap/memory files and treat arbitrary workspace edits as out of scope until a stronger product case exists.

options.title: Open System Browser Design
options.body: Create a separate security-reviewed host filesystem browser design with explicit operator opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only First
recommendation.body: Keep the current read-only workspace API, design workspace write/delete/move/upload as a reviewed `agents.workspace.*` contract, and defer system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current read-only workspace API direction and opened the related mobile workspace-browser design that split reads from broader mutations.
